subject: Critical Thinking
title: Deduction: From General to Specific
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Deduction: From General to Specific.

hook.text: All humans are mortal. Socrates is human. Therefore, Socrates is mortal. You just did deduction.

buildup.text: Deductive reasoning starts with general principles and applies them to specific cases.

discovery.text: If the premises are true and the logic is valid, the conclusion is guaranteed. 100% certain.

twist.text: This certainty is deduction's strength and weakness — it can only confirm what's already in the premises.

climax.text: Deduction is the backbone of mathematics, formal proofs, and legal reasoning.

punchline.text: Deduction never discovers anything new. It unpacks what's already there.

quiz.question: What direction does deductive reasoning move?

details.summary: Deductive reasoning moves from general premises to specific conclusions with logical certainty. If the premises are true and the form is valid, the conclusion must be true—making deduction the gold standard of logical proof.
details.whyItMatters: Deduction underpins mathematics, formal proofs, and any reasoning where certainty rather than probability is the goal.
takeaways: Valid deduction guarantees the conclusion if premises are true
It moves from general rules to specific cases
The form of the argument determines validity, not content

faq.question: What makes deductive reasoning different from other types of reasoning?
faq.answer: Deduction offers certainty: if the premises are true and the argument is valid, the conclusion cannot be false. Other reasoning types deal in probability.

faq.question: Can a deductive argument be valid but have a false conclusion?
faq.answer: Yes, if one or more premises are false. Validity means the conclusion follows from the premises, not that the premises are true. Sound arguments require both validity and true premises.
